about: The Carnet « Le sommaire » search as the phone runs it on its copy (`GET /v1/notebook/index`, sommaire.md §3 « The phone's search », plan §3.1–3.3): the same query gives the same results in HermesKit (CarnetSearch, CarnetSearchTests.theSearchFollowsTheParityFile), on Android (D1) and at the bridge (S3). Draft written from the phone's side with brick A1 (22/11), on the fake bridge's copies; S3 makes it the bridge's own (its rule, its copies, more cases, the bench's 270 queries mapped to the index's ids) and the three play it. A case names its copy (`index`, a file of this folder), its day (`today`, in `zone`) and its query (`q`, with `category`/`space` when the search is narrowed), then says any of: `first` (the first result's id), `top` (the first results, in order), `includes` / `excludes` (ids that must / must not be found), `found` (exactly these, any order), `count` (how many), `counts` (these chips' numbers), `groups` (the categories of the groups, in order, from the first), `interval` (the days of the query's date phrase), `terms` (what is looked for: each word's spellings, itself then its neighbours, each a list of words). Ids are the index's (`page:`, `line:<page>:<hash>`, `task:`, `record:`, `doc:`, `fam:list:`, `fam:page:`).
rule: fold the query as the bridge folds (`fold`, the cases of offline-parity.json): lower case, no accents (ß → ss, æ → ae, œ → oe, ø → o, ł → l, đ → d), anything not an ASCII letter or digit a space, spaces squeezed

a phrase of the copy's `dates.phrases` (folded, whole words, the longest first) becomes the interval from its `from` to its `to`, computed from today (`dates` below); the first phrase found only; taken out of the query
a key of `neighbours` of several words (folded, whole words, the longest first) becomes one term: its own words, or one of its neighbours; taken out of the query

the words left, without the copy's `stop` words unless nothing else is left (no term, no interval), each once; a word's neighbours (`neighbours`) are other spellings of it, found as themselves only; at most 12 terms
an item's words: its `fold` (its own), and around it its title, its source, its aliases and its page's (`page`), folded

a word typed is found as itself, as the start of a word from 3 letters, and with one typo from 5 letters, two from 8 (a letter added, removed, changed, or two side by side swapped: optimal string alignment); never a typo towards a word under 4 letters

kept: the items holding every term when there are some, else those holding at least one; with an interval, only those whose `date` is in it, or whose `yearly` day is in it in one of its years (a date phrase alone: every item dated in it); a category: items having it among theirs, `dates` as the phone adds it; a space (`perso`, `pro`; `all`: both): items of that space
Dates is the phone's to add (the copy never depends on the day): an item with a `yearly` day, or a `date` within `dated` (from `before` days ago to `after` days ahead, 90 and 730)

ranked: (0) an archived item (`archived`) after all the others; (1) not a line, and its folded title or an alias (a line: its page's too) is the whole folded query, or the query's words without its stop words and date phrase; (2) every term; (3) a direct answer: a word of a term in its folded `label`; (4) the number of terms, then how closely: per term the best of 2 × (itself 3, start of a word or neighbour 2, typo 1) + 1 when in its own words rather than around it; (5) the most recently noted (a page: its latest line's `noted`); (6) still to come: an open task, a `yearly` date, else a `date` from today; (7) the copy's order

grouped under each item's first category (`other` when none), the groups in the order of their best result, each with the notes listed under it and its two best; `counts`: `all` each note once, and each category every note having it (`dates` as the phone adds it)

dates: `day` today + n; `week` the ISO week n from this one (Monday first), its `start` or `end` (no edge: today + 7n days); `month` / `year` n from this one, the `start` or `end` (no edge: today + n); `feast` the copy's absolute day (`dates.feasts`), none: the phrase is not used; `weekday` (ISO, 1 Monday … 7 Sunday) the coming one, today included, + n weeks
